home.title: TypeScript business code first. Deployment and API later.
home.subtitle: Declare your domain once. Validation, tables, API and forms derive from it, and one config line decides where each part runs.
home.plateCredit: R. Siélain, Atlas de poche des plantes des champs, pl. 124, 1895
home.codeText: The green marble is your business code: plain classes that do the work and ask for what they need. No route, no setup, no server required.
home.schemaText: The yellow marble is your schema: you describe a post once, and your code uses it everywhere.
home.derivationText: The API, the validation, the form and the table are all read from your schema. Change a field and they change with it.
home.derivationCalls: Incoming — REST, GraphQL, forms, client types
home.derivationCaption: One field added to an entity: the table, the form and the API follow.
home.choicesText: One process or several, which implementation answers each port, SQLite or Postgres: each is one line in fougere.config.ts, completed by your editor from your own code. Your code does not change.
home.choicesCaption: One line in fougere.config.ts: the blog answers from its own process, and the page keeps working.
home.tryText: No table, no protocol, no host, no address. What it leaves out is derived from it, or chosen by you, and that is why it never had to change.
home.derivationDoc: Get forms and an API from your schema
home.auditTitle: Don't take our word for it.
home.auditText: Paste this prompt into the agent that already knows your codebase. It finds what your code declares twice and what that has cost you, then prices moving one module to Fougere, and what would get worse.
